topics: 🍇 How Do We Bless on Fruit? — the mishna opening the sixth chapter: tree, vine, ground, bread, vegetables
📜 Searching for a Source — 'kodesh hillulim', vineyard and grain, the seven species, and why every derivation fails
💡 It Is Simply Reasonable — one may not benefit from this world without a blessing; go to a Sage and learn
🌍 Whose Earth Is It? — 'The earth is the Lord's' vs. 'the earth He gave to mankind'; robbing father and mother

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Blessings Over Food Begin
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 35a–35b
overview.hebrewSource: אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּהָנֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא בְּרָכָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: A new chapter opens with the mishna that assigns a blessing to every category of food: borei peri ha'etz on tree fruit, borei peri hagafen on wine, borei peri ha'adama on produce of the ground, hamotzi on bread. The Gemara immediately asks where the Torah obligates a blessing before eating at all, and after chasing the verse 'sanctified for praises' through a maze of derivations, concludes that the obligation rests on reason: the world belongs to God, and enjoying it without a blessing is like misusing consecrated property. That thought spills into the famous debate over how a Jew should balance Torah study with earning a living. Finally the Gemara returns to the mishna and asks why wine, unlike olive oil, earned a blessing of its own.

slides.title: 🍇 The Mishna: One Blessing for Each Category
slides.subtitle: Two 'exceptions' are really upgrades for especially significant foods
rows: בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ — Who creates fruit of the tree
Default for anything growing on a tree
בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן — Who creates fruit of the vine
Exception: significant enough to get its own formula
בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה — Who creates fruit of the ground
Default for produce that does not grow on a tree
הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ — Who brings forth bread from the earth
Exception: bread's importance earns a distinct blessing
Rabbi Yehuda: בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי דְשָׁאִים, 'Who creates various kinds of herbs'

callout.label: Rabbi Yehuda's view:
callout.text: He sees a difference in quality between ordinary produce of the ground and leafy herbs, so he assigns herbs a formula of their own. The Rabbis lump them together under 'fruit of the ground'.

slides.title: 📜 Where Does the Torah Require a Blessing Before Eating?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara tries one derivation after another, and each one leaks

nodes.content: ❓ 'Sanctified for praises (הִלּוּלִים) before the Lord' (Lev. 19:24) — the plural teaches a blessing before and after. Rabbi Akiva: one may not taste anything before blessing.
⚠️ But that verse is already used: one hillul = ḥillul, 'redeem, then eat'; the other = only what needs song (wine libation, Judges 9:13) needs redemption

columns.label: Teaches 'fourth-year vineyard'
columns.content: If he learns 'vineyard' from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's gezera shava (תְּבוּאָתוֹ / תְּבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם), one hillul is left over for the blessing — but that gives only the blessing after; 'before' comes from a kal vaḥomer (if satiated he blesses, when hungry all the more so)

columns.label: Teaches 'fourth-year sapling'
columns.content: Works for anything planted — but meat, eggs and fish are not planted. Where is their blessing?

nodes.content: 🔁 Extending from vineyard to all foods also fails: vineyard is special (olelot), grain is special (ḥalla), their common denominator is 'offered on the altar', the seven species are special (bikkurim)
✅ Rather, it is sevara — reason itself: אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּהָנֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא בְּרָכָה, one may not benefit from this world without a blessing

callout.label: Side note:
callout.text: Rav Pappa closes a loophole in the derivation: an olive grove is called kerem zayit (Judges 15:5), never plain kerem, so the olive cannot ride on the vineyard's status.

slides.title: 🌍 Eating Without a Blessing: Three Descriptions of the Offense
slides.subtitle: The Amoraim reach for the language of sacrilege and theft

boxes.title: Me'ila — Misuse of Sanctity
items: Tosefta: whoever benefits without a blessing is as if he committed me'ila
Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: as if he enjoyed consecrated property of Heaven — 'The earth and all it contains is the Lord's' (Ps. 24:1)
Remedy? 'Go to a Sage.' Rava: go beforehand and let him teach you blessings, so you never come to me'ila

boxes.title: Rabbi Levi's Resolution
items: Contradiction: 'the earth is the Lord's' (Ps. 24:1) vs. 'the earth He gave to mankind' (Ps. 115:16)
Before a blessing — the earth is the Lord's
After a blessing — He has given it to mankind

boxes.title: Theft from Father and Mother
items: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa: as if he robs God and the community of Israel — 'Whoever robs his father and mother… is companion to a destroyer' (Prov. 28:24)
'Father' = God ('Is He not your Father Who created you', Deut. 32:6); 'mother' = Knesset Yisrael ('do not forsake the Torah of your mother', Prov. 1:8)
'Companion to a destroyer' = companion of Jeroboam ben Nevat, who corrupted Israel

callout.label: Grain, too:
callout.text: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa also reconciles 'I will take back My grain' (Hosea 2:11) with 'you shall gather your grain' (Deut. 11:14): the grain is theirs when Israel does God's will, His when they do not.

slides.title: 🌾 'You Shall Gather Your Grain' — Torah Study vs. Earning a Living
slides.subtitle: A tannaitic dispute, then the Amoraim weigh in with hard experience

lines.speaker: R' Yishmael
lines.text: 'This Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Josh. 1:8) could be read literally. So the Torah adds 'you shall gather your grain' — conduct yourself in the way of the world: Torah and work.

lines.speaker: R' Shimon b.Y.
lines.text: Plow in plowing season, sow, harvest, thresh, winnow — what will become of Torah? When Israel does God's will, 'strangers will stand and feed your flocks' (Isa. 61:5). 'Gather your grain' describes a time when they do not.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: Many did as Rabbi Yishmael and it succeeded for them; many did as Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai and it did not succeed for them.

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: To his students: I beg you, in Nisan and Tishrei do not appear before me, so that you are not preoccupied with your livelihood the whole year.

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: In the name of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi El'ai: the earlier generations made Torah fixed and work occasional, and both endured. The later generations made work fixed and Torah occasional, and neither endured.

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: Likewise, earlier generations brought produce in through the front gate to obligate it in tithes; later ones bring it through roofs and courtyards to exempt it. (Rabbi Yannai: tithes take hold only when produce 'sees the front of the house'; Rabbi Yoḥanan himself: even a courtyard fixes it.)

callout.label: Connection:
callout.text: The verse 'you shall gather your grain' entered the discussion to explain who owns the grain; the Gemara follows it into the question of how much of life belongs to the field.

slides.title: 🍷 Why Does Wine Get 'Fruit of the Vine' While Olive Oil Does Not?
slides.subtitle: Every proposed distinction between wine and oil is tested against a source

steps.content: 1️⃣ Proposal: wine's fruit was changed for the better, so its blessing changed. Objection: olive oil also changed for the better, yet Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan rule its blessing stays borei peri ha'etz
2️⃣ Answer: no fitting formula exists for oil — 'fruit of the olive' names the olive itself. Objection: say 'fruit of the olive tree'!

3️⃣ Mar Zutra: wine nourishes (זָיֵין), oil does not. Objection: one who vows off 'nourishment' is permitted only water and salt, so everything else, oil included, nourishes (Rav Huna reads that vow as 'anything that nourishes')
4️⃣ Rather: wine satisfies (סָעֵיד), oil does not. Objection: Rava drank wine all Passover eve to whet his appetite for matza! Answer: a lot stimulates, a little satisfies

5️⃣ Objection: 'wine gladdens the heart of man… and bread satisfies' (Ps. 104:15) — bread satisfies, not wine! Answer: wine has two virtues, it satisfies and it gladdens; bread satisfies but does not gladden

6️⃣ Then recite the three blessings of Grace after wine? People do not base a meal on it. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: and if one does? Rava: when Elijah comes he will tell us; for now his intention is nullified by everyone else's

callout.label: Olive oil itself:
callout.text: When is borei peri ha'etz said over oil? Not when drunk plain — that harms (one who drinks teruma oil pays the principal but not the fifth), and not when dipped with bread, where the bread is primary and exempts the oil. The Gemara turns to oil taken in anigeron, beet water, and the discussion continues on the next daf.

summary.principle: No verse fully sources the blessing before food; it stands on reason — the world is God's until a blessing releases it to us — and that same conviction shapes how wine, oil, and even a day's work are understood.

flowSteps.content: 📖 Mishna: tree fruit → ha'etz; wine → hagafen; ground → ha'adama; bread → hamotzi; vegetables → ha'adama (R' Yehuda: minei deshaim)
❓ Source for a blessing before eating? 'Kodesh hillulim', gezera shava, kal vaḥomer, common denominators, seven species — each fails (meat, eggs, fish!)
💡 Sevara: forbidden to benefit from this world without a blessing; doing so is me'ila, theft from Father and Mother. Rava: learn blessings from a Sage in advance

columns.content: 🌍 Ps. 24:1 before a blessing; Ps. 115:16 after. 'Gather your grain' → R' Yishmael vs. R' Shimon b. Yoḥai; Abaye: R' Yishmael's way succeeded
🍷 Wine vs. oil: wine both satisfies and gladdens, so it earns hagafen; still no Grace after Meals, since people do not base meals on it

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: A blessing is the act that turns God's property into ours — before it, 'the earth is the Lord's'; after it, 'the earth He gave to mankind'

quiz.q: After all the attempted derivations, what does the Gemara conclude is the basis for reciting a blessing before eating?
o: The verse 'sanctified for praises' (Leviticus 19:24)
A verbal analogy between fourth-year fruit and the vineyard
Reason (sevara): one may not benefit from this world without a blessing
The obligation of first fruits from the seven species
quiz.e: Each scriptural derivation fails — most tellingly, none covers meat, eggs, and fish. The Gemara therefore rests the obligation on sevara: it is forbidden to benefit from this world without a blessing.

quiz.q: How does Rabbi Levi resolve the contradiction between 'The earth and all it contains is the Lord's' and 'The earth He has given to mankind'?
o: One verse speaks of Eretz Yisrael, the other of the rest of the world
One verse refers to before a blessing, the other to after a blessing
One verse refers to when Israel does God's will, the other to when they do not
One verse refers to the heavens, the other to the earth
quiz.e: Before a blessing the earth is the Lord's; after a blessing He has given it to mankind. (The 'doing God's will' distinction is Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa's answer to a different contradiction, about grain.)

quiz.q: According to Rava, what does 'go to a Sage' mean as a remedy for one who benefited without a blessing?
o: The Sage will impose a fine equal to the value of what was eaten
The Sage will recite the blessing on his behalf after the fact
He should go to a Sage beforehand and learn the blessings so he never comes to misuse
He should confess the misuse before the Sage
quiz.e: The Gemara objects that a Sage cannot undo a violation already committed. Rava explains: go to a Sage from the outset and learn blessings, so that you do not come to me'ila.

quiz.q: What did Abaye observe about the dispute between Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai?
o: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai because Torah must be one's sole occupation
Many who followed Rabbi Yishmael's path succeeded, while many who followed Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's did not
Both approaches succeeded equally for those who tried them
Rabbi Yishmael's view applies only in Nisan and Tishrei
quiz.e: Abaye reports that many acted like Rabbi Yishmael, combining work and Torah, and succeeded, whereas many who tried Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's approach of Torah alone did not succeed.

quiz.q: What is the Gemara's final explanation for why wine, unlike olive oil, receives its own blessing?
o: Wine nourishes while oil does not
There is no suitable blessing formula for oil
Wine both satisfies and gladdens, whereas bread only satisfies and oil does neither in this way
Wine is used for song in the Temple
quiz.e: 'Nourishes' fails because oil also counts as nourishment, and 'satisfies' alone is challenged from Psalms 104:15. The resolution is that wine has two virtues, it satisfies and it gladdens, while bread satisfies without gladdening.
